items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee narrates a story about Elmer Snowden, Sonny Greer, and Duke Ellington ('He had raised Elmer, give Elmer the raise and Elmer didn't give it to the guys, so they fired Elmer...'), but does not claim a personal relationship with Snowden.

ctx.x: Elmer Snowden,yeah. So Sonny, you know how Sonny talk and says, man, when you going to give us a raise. And the man said I just raised you. He had raised Elmer, give Elmer the raise and Elmer didn't give it to the guys, so they fired Elmer and Sonny was supposed to take the job, Sonny said no, I don't want the job. Give it to Duke. And that's when Duke took over.
And that was a trio. Duke Ellington on piano, Sonny Greer on drums and Elmer Snowden on banjo.

items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: And you played this with Mitch Elmer?

ctx.x: Violinist, that's right. He'd come down there and bring his violin and say, now, I'm going to fool around and break all my strings until I get down to the G string. When the G string -- this is the end of a perfect day.
And you played this with Mitch Elmer?

items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: Caruso, Eddie Cantor, Mission Elmer. ... He'd come down there and bring his violin

ctx.x: And I said, yeah. So I went down there and made an audition for the guy and the guy says, all right, the job is yours. Caruso, Eddie Cantor, Mission Elmer.

Violinist, that's right. He'd come down there and bring his violin and say, now, I'm going to fool around and break all my strings until I get down to the G string. When the G string -- this is the end of a perfect day.
